simple.meaning: נָחַץ (nâchats) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be urgent.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 21:9. Its contexts include death, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָחַץ (H5169).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָחַץ (nâchats) / H5169 is traced through 1 Samuel 21:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5169. nachats [ נָחַץ ] verb urge (?), whence (si vera lectio); — Qal Passive participle ( active Participle in u , according to Ba NB 175 ), נָחוּץ הַמֶּל֛ח דְּבַד 1Sam 21:9 the king's business was urgent ( ᵐ5 κατὰ σπουδήν , A κατασπεῦδον ). (Thes compare Arabic ursit instititgue rogando [Kam Frey]); text dubious; HPS נָאוֺץ (from אוץ ), > נחושׁ . נחר (probably onomatopoetic √ of following; compare Assyrian na—îru , nostril ; Arabic snort , nostril ; Ethiopic snort ; Syriac id. , nostril ; נְחִירָא ᵑ7 id. ; also Late Hebrew Pi`el snort ). — נָחַר Jer 6:29 etc., see I. חרר .
